library(nlmixr2lib)

# Models and source

Hoeben 2026 builds a translational framework for the PEGylated
L-asparaginase calaspargase pegol (CalPEG) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
A Simeoni tumor-growth-inhibition (TGI) model is fitted to JHH-5 xenograft
mice, driven by a mouse PK model of plasma asparaginase activity (PAA); the
TGI parameters are then linked to the population PK model of PAA fitted in
patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) to predict tumor response in
adults with HCC. The paper therefore contributes two model files and this one
vignette.

```{r models}
modMouse <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hoeben_2026_calaspargasePegol_mouse_tgi"))
modHuman <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hoeben_2026_calaspargasePegol_human_tgi"))
```

* Citation: `r modMouse$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s13318-026-01010-4>
* Supplement: Electronic Supplementary Material 1 of the article (Tables
  S1-S5, Figures S1-S7), distributed with the PubMed Central record
  `PMC13558373`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Hoeben_2026_calaspargasePegol_mouse_tgi` | Mouse PAA model (fixed from an earlier mouse PK analysis) + Simeoni TGI fitted to JHH-5 xenografts |
| `Hoeben_2026_calaspargasePegol_human_tgi` | Human PAA model fitted in ALL (BSA, sex and age covariates) + the xenograft TGI parameters |

# Population

**Mice.** 40 female BALB/c nude mice bearing subcutaneous JHH-5 HCC
xenografts (an ASNS promoter-hypermethylated line), 10 per group, received
vehicle or 20, 40 or 100 IU/kg CalPEG IV every 4 days for 28 days (8 doses;
Methods "Data Collection", Supplementary Table S1). The mean tumor volume at
the start of treatment was 175 mm^3. The fit used 527 tumor volumes and 87 PAA
samples. The PK sub-model had been estimated earlier on 344 PAA samples from
90 non-grafted and grafted mice (6-300 IU/kg, Supplementary Table S2) and was
held fixed.

**Humans.** The PK model was fitted to 1680 PAA observations from 144
patients with ALL in three studies (AALL07P4, N = 111; DFCI-11-001, N = 13;
CL2-95015-001, N = 20) dosed at 1000-2500 IU/m^2 (Supplementary Table S3A).
Age ranged 1-73 years (median 12.5), BSA 0.42-2.80 m^2 (median 1.47), weight
8.45-152 kg (median 48.5); 51% were female and 81% White (Supplementary
Tables S3B-S3C). The HCC predictions simulate a 55-year-old man (BSA
2.05 m^2) and woman (BSA 1.81 m^2) receiving 500-2500 IU/m^2 as a 2-h
infusion every 3 weeks.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Hoeben_2026_calaspargasePegol_human_tgi")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse PK: `dAc/dt = -Vmax*Ac*Ae/(Km*V + Ac)`, `dAe/dt = kout*(1 - Aspa/(Aspa + EC50)) - kout*Ae`, `Ae(0) = 1` | -- | Supplementary Figure S1B |
| `lvc` (mouse V) | 0.0636 L/kg (IIV SD 0.0765) | Table 1, Mice PK |
| `lvmax` (mouse Vm) | 5.07 IU/kg/h (IIV SD 0.164) | Table 1, Mice PK |
| `lkm` (mouse Km) | 4000 IU/L (IIV SD 0.0625) | Table 1, Mice PK |
| `lkout` | 0.000813 1/h | Table 1, Mice PK |
| `lec50` | 107 IU/L | Table 1, Mice PK |
| TGI: `dTS/dt = kg*TS/(1 + (kg/kgl*TS)^psi)^(1/psi) - Ed*TS`, three dying-cell transits at `1/tau` | -- | Equations 1-2 |
| `Ed = slp * PAA` (linear) | -- | Methods, Results "PKPD TGI Modeling" |
| `ltumorExpGrowth` (kg) | 0.00708 1/h (IIV SD 0.224) | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI |
| `ltumorLinGrowth` (kgl) | 70.0 mm^3/h | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI |
| `ldrugSlope` (slp) | 3.22e-5 L/IU/h (IIV SD 0.359) | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI |
| `ldamageTransit` (1/tau) | 1/41.1 1/h | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI (tau = 41.1 h) |
| `lrbase_tumor` (W0) | 152 mm^3 (IIV SD 0.114) | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI |
| `psi` | 20 (fixed) | Table 1, Mice PKPD TGI |
| `addSd_tumor_vol`, `propSd_tumor_vol` | 0.827 mm^3, 0.437 | Table 1, RUV1 / RUV2 |
| Human PK structure: linear CL + saturable Vmax/Km elimination, saturable VmaxTR/KmTR transfer to the periphery, k21 return | -- | Methods "PK Model in Pediatric and Adult Patients with ALL"; Figure 5 |
| `lvc`, `lcl` | 1.78 L (IIV SD 0.150), 0.00245 L/h (IIV SD 0.441) | Table 1, Human PK |
| `lvmax_tr`, `lkm_tr` | 21.4 IU/h, 58.8 IU/L | Table 1, Human PK |
| `lk21` | 0.0395 1/h (IIV SD 0.519; corr. with CL 0.582) | Table 1, Human PK |
| `lvmax`, `lkm` | 0.583 IU/h, 0.00100 IU/L | Table 1, Human PK |
| `e_bsa_vc`, `e_bsa_cl`, `e_bsa_vmax_tr`, `e_bsa_vmax` | 1.23, 1.19, 0.726, 1.24 | Table 1, Human PK |
| `e_sexf_vc` | -0.0928 | Table 1, Human PK ("Female on Vc") |
| `e_age_vmax` | -0.0166 1/year | Table 1, Human PK ("AGE on Vmax") |
| BSA normalised to 1.47 m^2 | -- | Supplementary Table S3B (dataset median); see Assumptions |
| Human TGI parameters | as mouse, fixed | Results "PKPD Translation to Humans"; Figure 5 |

# Mouse PK and tumor growth inhibition

The xenograft design: Q4D IV doses on days 0-28 (8 doses), 200 virtual mice
per arm.

```{r mouse-events}
n_mouse <- 200
mouse_doses <- c(0, 20, 40, 100)
obs_mouse <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 672, by = 4), c(96, 192, 288, 384, 672) - 5 / 60)))
make_mouse <- function(dose, arm) {
  ids <- (arm - 1) * n_mouse + seq_len(n_mouse)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_mouse) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  if (dose > 0) {
    dosing <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 672, by = 96)) |>
      mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
    obs <- bind_rows(dosing, obs)
  }
  obs |> mutate(dose_grp = dose)
}
ev_mouse <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mouse_doses), function(i) make_mouse(mouse_doses[i], i))) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_mouse <- rxSolve(modMouse, ev_mouse, keep = "dose_grp", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(day = time / 24, dose_lab = factor(paste(dose_grp, "IU/kg"), levels = paste(mouse_doses, "IU/kg")))
```

## PAA in the xenograft study (Figure 1)

The Discussion reports the predicted median predose PAA on day 12 as 71.3,
167 and 596 IU/L at 20, 40 and 100 IU/kg.

```{r mouse-day12}
day12 <- sim_mouse |>
  filter(dose_grp > 0, abs(time - (288 - 5 / 60)) < 1e-6) |>
  group_by(dose_grp) |>
  summarise(simulated = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(published = c(71.3, 167, 596), pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(day12) == 3)
knitr::kable(day12 |> rename("Dose (IU/kg)" = dose_grp, "Simulated median (IU/L)" = simulated,
  "Published median (IU/L)" = published, "% difference" = pct_diff), digits = 1)
# PK IIV is small (SD <= 0.164), so the medians are stable across cohorts
# (realised 2-7%). A wrong volume, Km or dose unit moves them by > 50%.
stopifnot(all(abs(day12$pct_diff) < 15))
```

```{r mouse-fig1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Hoeben 2026: PAA median and 90% prediction interval in the JHH-5 xenograft study."}
sim_mouse |>
  filter(dose_grp > 0, time > 0) |>
  group_by(dose_lab, day) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose_lab) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "PAA (IU/L)")
```

## Tumor volume (Figure 3)

The minimal PAA for tumor regression is `CT = kg / slp`; the paper reports
220 IU/L.

```{r mouse-ct}
ct <- exp(modMouse$theta[["ltumorExpGrowth"]]) / exp(modMouse$theta[["ldrugSlope"]])
ct
stopifnot(abs(ct - 220) < 1)
```

```{r mouse-fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Hoeben 2026: tumor volume median and 90% prediction interval by dose."}
tv_mouse <- sim_mouse |>
  group_by(dose_lab, dose_grp, day) |>
  summarise(med = median(tumor_vol), lo = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.05), hi = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(tv_mouse, aes(day, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(lo, 0.1), ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose_lab) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)")
```

The typical-value trajectories are compared with simulated medians read
from Figure 3 by the maintainers (vehicle about 1100 mm^3 on day 12; 20 IU/kg
about 430 mm^3 on day 28; 40 IU/kg about 10 mm^3 on day 28; 100 IU/kg about
15 mm^3 on day 12).

```{r mouse-fig3-check}
# One subject per solve: a multi-subject solve of a zeroRe() model warns.
typ_mouse <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 1, 2, 3) * n_mouse + 1, function(i) {
  rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(modMouse), ev_mouse |> filter(id == i), keep = "dose_grp", returnType = "data.frame")
}))
fig3 <- data.frame(dose_grp = c(0, 20, 40, 100), time = c(288, 672, 672, 288), figure = c(1100, 430, 10, 15)) |>
  left_join(typ_mouse |> select(dose_grp, time, tumor_vol), by = c("dose_grp", "time")) |>
  mutate(ratio = tumor_vol / figure)
stopifnot(nrow(fig3) == 4, !anyNA(fig3$tumor_vol))
knitr::kable(fig3 |> rename("Dose (IU/kg)" = dose_grp, "Time (h)" = time, "Figure 3 (mm^3)" = figure,
  "Typical value (mm^3)" = tumor_vol, "Ratio" = ratio), digits = 2)
# Deterministic; the figure values are read by eye from a log-scale panel.
stopifnot(all(abs(log(fig3$ratio)) < log(1.5)))
```

## Mouse NCA (first dosing interval)

```{r mouse-nca}
conc_mouse <- sim_mouse |>
  filter(dose_grp > 0, time <= 96, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_grp, "IU/kg")) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_mouse <- ev_mouse |>
  filter(evid == 1, time == 0) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose_grp, "IU/kg")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
nca_mouse <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_mouse, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCAdose(dose_mouse, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 96, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_mouse))
```

The paper reports no NCA for the mice; the table documents the first-interval
exposure of the packaged model. Cmax rises roughly in proportion to dose
(Km = 4000 IU/L is far above the concentrations reached), while the troughs
rise more than proportionally because the enzyme pool that eliminates
CalPEG is depleted faster at higher PAA.

# Human PK in HCC patients (Table 2, Supplementary Table S4)

## Dose convention used by the published simulations

The model takes the dose as an amount in IU (IU/m^2 x BSA), the form in which
the ALL data were fitted. The paper's simulated exposure tables are
reproduced, for both sexes at once, only when the simulated amount equals the
**nominal per-m^2 number** (500 IU for "500 IU/m^2"). Scaling by BSA instead
doubles every concentration and gets the male-to-female ratio wrong:

```{r dose-convention}
cinf_check <- function(sexf, bsa, amt) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1, time = c(0, 2), evid = c(1L, 0L), amt = c(amt, 0), dur = c(2, NA),
    cmt = "central", dvid = c(NA, 1L), BSA = bsa, SEXF = sexf, AGE = 55)
  sim <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(modHuman), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  sim$Cc[sim$time == 2]
}
conv <- data.frame(
  Sex = c("Male", "Female"), BSA = c(2.05, 1.81), published = c(188, 241)
) |>
  mutate(
    nominal = mapply(cinf_check, c(0, 1), BSA, 500),
    bsa_scaled = mapply(cinf_check, c(0, 1), BSA, 500 * BSA)
  )
knitr::kable(conv |> rename("BSA (m^2)" = BSA, "Published Cinf, dose 1 (IU/L)" = published,
  "Typical Cinf, 500 IU (IU/L)" = nominal, "Typical Cinf, 500 x BSA IU (IU/L)" = bsa_scaled), digits = c(0, 2, 0, 0, 0))
stopifnot(
  all(abs(conv$nominal / conv$published - 1) < 0.10),
  all(conv$bsa_scaled / conv$published > 1.7)
)
```

The comparisons below therefore follow the paper's convention. Use the
BSA-scaled amount to simulate the clinical regimen as labelled.

## Exposure after the 1st, 3rd and 5th dose

200 virtual 55-year-old men (BSA 2.05 m^2) and 200 women (BSA 1.81 m^2) per
dose level, 2-h infusions every 3 weeks.

```{r human-events}
n_human <- 200
human_doses <- c(500, 750, 1000, 1250, 1500, 2000, 2500)
tau <- 504
obs_human <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168 * 24, by = 12), tau * (0:7) + 2, tau * (0:7) + 1, tau * (0:7) + 6)))
make_human <- function(dose, sexf, arm, scale_bsa = FALSE) {
  bsa <- if (sexf == 1) 1.81 else 2.05
  amt <- if (scale_bsa) dose * bsa else dose
  ids <- (arm - 1) * n_human + seq_len(n_human)
  dosing <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = tau * (0:7)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = amt, dur = 2, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_human) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = NA_real_, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    mutate(dose_grp = dose, SEXF = sexf, BSA = bsa, AGE = 55)
}
arms <- expand.grid(dose = human_doses, sexf = c(0, 1))
ev_human <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) make_human(arms$dose[i], arms$sexf[i], i))) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_human <- rxSolve(modHuman, ev_human, keep = c("dose_grp", "SEXF"), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male"), day = time / 24)
```

Each administration is analysed as its own 0-504 h interval (time re-anchored
to the start of the dose), so PKNCA returns Cinf as `cmax`, Ctrough as
`ctrough` and Cavg as `cav`.

```{r human-nca}
conc_human <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 3, 5), function(k) {
  start <- tau * (k - 1)
  sim_human |>
    filter(time >= start, time <= start + tau, !is.na(Cc)) |>
    mutate(time = time - start, admin = k)
})) |>
  distinct(id, admin, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(sex, dose_grp)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, sex, dose_grp, admin, treatment)
nca_human <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_human, Cc ~ time | sex + dose_grp + admin + treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
))

published <- data.frame(
  sex = rep(c("Male", "Female"), each = 7),
  dose_grp = rep(human_doses, 2),
  t1 = c(19.3, 43.6, 76.3, 109, 149, 235, 326, 26.8, 57.2, 95.9, 137, 184, 291, 409),
  i1 = c(188, 283, 385, 481, 573, 780, 959, 241, 365, 494, 617, 745, 994, 1255),
  a1 = c(46.3, 90.1, 146, 201, 260, 391, 519, 60.8, 119, 186, 258, 334, 497, 670),
  t3 = c(57.2, 133, 219, 312, 397, 590, 743, 78.6, 167, 267, 368, 472, 687, 918),
  i3 = c(232, 383, 554, 722, 879, 1251, 1562, 305, 495, 704, 910, 1125, 1553, 2012),
  a3 = c(103, 220, 348, 478, 599, 871, 1104, 143, 282, 440, 588, 749, 1053, 1390),
  t5 = c(83.9, 177, 276, 378, 472, 691, 851, 111, 211, 321, 423, 547, 780, 1046),
  i5 = c(267, 450, 651, 849, 1032, 1455, 1796, 350, 577, 809, 1040, 1277, 1751, 2280),
  a5 = c(140, 287, 428, 578, 706, 1029, 1269, 188, 354, 520, 688, 857, 1198, 1576)
) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(sex, dose_grp), names_to = c(".value", "admin"), names_pattern = "([tia])([135])") |>
  transmute(sex, dose_grp, admin = as.numeric(admin), ctrough = t, cmax = i, cav = a)

cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(nca_human, published, by = c("sex", "dose_grp", "admin"),
  params = c("cmax", "ctrough", "cav"))
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

```{r human-nca-check}
sim_med <- as.data.frame(nca_human$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "ctrough", "cav")) |>
  group_by(sex, dose_grp, admin, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
chk <- published |>
  pivot_longer(c(cmax, ctrough, cav), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref") |>
  inner_join(sim_med, by = c("sex", "dose_grp", "admin", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == 126, !anyNA(chk$sim))
summary(chk$pct_diff)
# Structural: a wrong BSA normalisation, sex or age form, or dose convention
# moves the whole table by 10-100% (see the dose-convention chunk and the
# age-form comparison below). Envelope on a robust quantile, not the extremes.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 12,
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25
)
```

The simulated medians sit a few percent below the published ones (median
difference about -6%, range about -22% to +4%; Cinf is about 5% low
throughout). See Assumptions and deviations.

```{r human-fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Hoeben 2026: PAA median and 90% prediction interval in men (BSA 2.05 m^2, 55 years); red line = 100 IU/L."}
sim_human |>
  filter(sex == "Male", time > 0) |>
  group_by(dose_grp, day) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose_grp, "IU/m^2 Q3W")) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "PAA (IU/L)")
```

# Human tumor-growth predictions (Figure 6)

```{r human-fig6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Hoeben 2026 (men): tumor volume median and 90% prediction interval; red line = 90% regression from 152 mm^3."}
tv_human <- sim_human |>
  group_by(sex, dose_grp, day) |>
  summarise(med = median(tumor_vol), lo = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.05), hi = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
tv_human |>
  filter(sex == "Male") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = pmin(hi, 3000)), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15.2, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose_grp, "IU/m^2 Q3W")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 3000)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)")
```

Day on which the median tumor volume first falls to 10% of the 152 mm^3
baseline (`NA` = not within 168 days). The paper reports, for men, complete
regression at 750 IU/m^2 after the 5th dose (days 84-105), at 1000 IU/m^2
after the 3rd (days 42-63) and at 1250 IU/m^2 between the 2nd and 3rd
(days 21-42).

```{r human-regression}
first_day <- function(day, med) {
  hit <- day[med <= 0.1 * 152]
  if (length(hit) == 0) NA_real_ else min(hit)
}
reg <- tv_human |>
  group_by(sex, dose_grp) |>
  summarise(day_90pct = first_day(day, med), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = day_90pct)
knitr::kable(reg |> rename("Dose (IU/m^2)" = dose_grp), digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  nrow(reg) == 7,
  # At 500 IU/m^2 the average PAA stays below the 220 IU/L threshold
  # (Table 2 Cavg <= 140 IU/L), so the tumor never regresses (Figure 6).
  is.na(reg$Male[reg$dose_grp == 500]),
  # 2500 IU/m^2 regresses within the first two cycles in both sexes.
  reg$Male[reg$dose_grp == 2500] < 42, reg$Female[reg$dose_grp == 2500] < 42
)
```

The model reaches 90% regression later than Figure 6 shows at 750-1250
IU/m^2. This is not resolvable from the published values: with the paper's own
Table 2 exposures (Cavg 90, 220 and 287 IU/L after the 1st, 3rd and 5th
750 IU/m^2 dose) and its kg and slp (threshold 220 IU/L), the typical tumor
grows about eightfold during the first cycle and is still above baseline at
day 84 (a hand calculation over the five cycles), whereas Figure 6 shows a median peak near 1000 mm^3 and regression by
day 84. The Figure 6 simulations therefore used higher exposure than the
Table 2 simulations; see Assumptions and deviations.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **BSA normalisation (1.47 m^2).** Neither the paper nor the 2018 FDA review
  of the earlier model version states the value BSA is normalised to. The
  model uses 1.47 m^2, the median of the 144-subject PK dataset
  (Supplementary Table S3B). With the paper's dose convention (next item),
  this value reproduces the published first-dose Cinf for men and women
  (188 and 241 IU/L) together.
* **Dose convention of the published simulations.** Table 2 and
  Supplementary Table S4 are reproduced only when the simulated amount equals
  the nominal per-m^2 number (500 IU for 500 IU/m^2). The model itself takes
  the dose in IU, the form in which the ALL data were fitted; multiply the
  per-m^2 dose by BSA to simulate a labelled regimen.
* **Age effect on Vmax: uncentred exponential.** Table 1 gives "AGE on Vmax =
  -0.0166" without the functional form or a centring value. The model uses
  `Vmax * exp(-0.0166 * AGE)`. The maintainers compared this with an
  exponential centred on the 12.5-year dataset median and with a linear form
  centred on the median (which would make Vmax negative for the 73-year-old
  oldest patient). Against Table 2 and Supplementary Table S4, the uncentred
  form reproduces the trough PAA closely (within about 4% after the 1st, 3rd
  and 5th 500 IU/m^2 dose in men); median centring puts the troughs about 20%
  lower. The chunk below makes the comparison on a paired cohort.
* **Sex effect.** "Female on Vc = -0.0928" is encoded as
  `Vc * (1 - 0.0928 * SEXF)`; an exponential form differs by less than 0.5%.
* **Residual error not reported.** The proportional residual error of both
  PK models is named but not quantified, so `propSd` is `fixed(0)` in both
  files; the tumor-volume error (additive 0.827 mm^3, proportional 0.437) is
  that of the xenograft fit and is carried unchanged into the human file.
* **Tumor volume = replicating + dying cells.** Equation 1 uses the
  replicating cells TS in the exponential-to-linear switch, as printed; the
  observed volume is the sum of TS and the three dying-cell stages (Simeoni
  2004). This reproduces the Figure 3 VPC medians.
* **Human TGI.** The human file carries the xenograft TGI parameters,
  including their IIV, as fixed values, and starts every tumor at 152 mm^3,
  as the paper did. Figure 6 is not reproduced at 750-1250 IU/m^2 (see the
  previous section).
* **Not packaged.** The re-estimation of the TGI model with the M3 method for
  values below 1 mm^3 (Supplementary Table S5) is a sensitivity analysis; the
  final model is the one in Table 1.

```{r age-form}
# Paired cohort: the same base-R eta draws for both age forms, passed as data
# columns, so the comparison carries no between-cohort noise.
set.seed(20261117)
om <- modHuman$omega[c("etalvc", "etalcl", "etalk21"), c("etalvc", "etalcl", "etalk21")]
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_human * 3), n_human) %*% chol(om)
colnames(eta) <- colnames(om)
ev_age <- bind_rows(
  expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_human), time = tau * (0:4)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 500, dur = 2, dvid = NA_integer_),
  expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_human), time = c(1, 3, 5) * tau) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = NA_real_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", BSA = 2.05, SEXF = 0, AGE = 55,
    etaltumorExpGrowth = 0, etaldrugSlope = 0, etalrbase_tumor = 0) |>
  left_join(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_human), eta), by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
troughs <- function(mod) {
  rxSolve(mod, ev_age, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(median_trough = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(published = c(19.3, 57.2, 83.9))
}
# Median centring is equivalent to scaling Vmax by exp(0.0166 * 12.5).
modCentred <- modHuman |> rxode2::ini(lvmax = log(0.583 * exp(0.0166 * 12.5)))
age_cmp <- bind_rows(
  troughs(modHuman) |> mutate(form = "Uncentred (packaged)"),
  troughs(modCentred) |> mutate(form = "Centred on 12.5 years")
) |>
  mutate(admin = time / tau, pct_diff = 100 * (median_trough / published - 1))
knitr::kable(age_cmp |> select(form, admin, median_trough, published, pct_diff) |>
  rename("Age form" = form, "Administration" = admin, "Simulated median Ctrough (IU/L)" = median_trough,
    "Table 2 (IU/L)" = published, "% difference" = pct_diff), digits = 1)
err <- age_cmp |> group_by(form) |> summarise(mae = mean(abs(pct_diff)))
stopifnot(nrow(age_cmp) == 6, err$mae[err$form == "Uncentred (packaged)"] < err$mae[err$form == "Centred on 12.5 years"])
```
